title: Balanced scalar comparisons with quotient and transition squares
statement:
Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme isomorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the small pro-etale sites and compatible small skeletons in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention], and write $F=g^{-1}$ for inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], sheafified balanced tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and cochain complexes with the direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].

For $W=X,Y$ let $j_W:R_W\to S_W$ be a map of commutative ring sheaves, and for $m\geq1$ let $A_{W,m},B_{W,m}$ be commutative ring sheaves with transitions $q^A,q^B$, maps $i_{W,m}:A_{W,m}\to B_{W,m}$ and maps $\pi^A_{W,m}:R_W\to A_{W,m}$, $\pi^B_{W,m}:S_W\to B_{W,m}$. Assume $q^Bi_{m+1}=i_mq^A$, the projections commute with transitions, and $\pi^B_{W,m}j_W=i_{W,m}\pi^A_{W,m}$. Let $c_R:FR_Y\simeq R_X$, $c_S:FS_Y\simeq S_X$, $c_{A,m}:FA_{Y,m}\simeq A_{X,m}$, $c_{B,m}:FB_{Y,m}\simeq B_{X,m}$ be ring isomorphisms commuting with $j,i,\pi$ and transitions. Let $G_R,G_S,G_{A,m},G_{B,m}$ mean $F$ with the respective transported scalar actions. For an arbitrary $R_Y$-complex $P$, let
$$b_P:G_RP\otimes_{R_X}S_X\xrightarrow{\sim}G_S(P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y)$$
be the balanced comparison normalized by $Fp\otimes c_S(Fs)\mapsto F(p\otimes s)$.

There are natural $B_{X,m}$-linear isomorphisms of complexes
$$b_{P,m}:G_{A,m}(P\otimes_{R_Y}A_{Y,m})\otimes_{A_{X,m}}B_{X,m}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{B,m}(P\otimes_{R_Y}B_{Y,m})$$
with mutually inverse local rules
$$F(p\otimes a)\otimes t\longmapsto F\bigl(p\otimes i_{Y,m}(a)c_{B,m}^{-1}(t)\bigr),\qquad F(p\otimes u)\longmapsto F(p\otimes1)\otimes c_{B,m}(Fu).$$
In these formulas local sections on corresponding objects are identified through $F$; in particular $c_{B,m}^{-1}(t)$ is read on the corresponding $Y$ object.

The left and right coefficient maps
$$v_m(Fp\otimes s)=F(p\otimes1)\otimes\pi^B_{X,m}(s),\qquad w_m(F(p\otimes s_0))=F(p\otimes\pi^B_{Y,m}(s_0))$$
are chain maps and satisfy $b_{P,m}v_m=w_mb_P$. After restriction to $S_X$ along $\pi^B_{X,m}$, let $t_m$ and $u_m$ be the transitions on these finite source and target complexes induced by $q^A,q^B$. They satisfy $b_{P,m}t_m=u_mb_{P,m+1}$. All these maps commute with differentials and are natural for chain maps $P\to P'$. No projection or transition is required to be surjective and no coefficient map is required to be flat.

proof.text: Use the normalized extensionAdjunction of def-pur-cochain-coefficient-arrows. Compose two adjunctions and identify restriction along a composite ring map with successive restrictions. Uniqueness of left adjoints gives scalar reassociation. Evaluating the hom-equivalence on the normalized units proves z tensor (a tensor p) maps to z*i(a) tensor p.

source.place: Tags 03CY and 03EK; normalized extension/restriction adjunction and balanced scalar extension.

proof.text: Use the corresponding-object site equivalence to construct the module equivalence, exactly as in isoSectionwiseModuleInverseImage_exact. The ring isomorphisms and coefficient square identify scalar restriction before and after inverse image. Transpose this restriction square along the two scalar-extension adjunctions. This mate is invertible: precomposition with it induces bijections on morphisms into the essential image of the target equivalence. Its pure-tensor rule follows from the normalized units and the inverse coefficient action.

source.place: Tags 03CY and 03EK; normalized extension/restriction adjunction and balanced scalar extension.

proof.text: Compose the transported scalar isomorphism for i with reassociation for piA followed by i, using j followed by piB = piA followed by i. This gives bfin and its forward local formula. Apply the inverse to that formula with a=1 and s=cB(u), and cancel hom followed by inverse, to obtain the stated inverse local formula.

source.place: Tags 03CY and 03EK; normalized extension/restriction adjunction and balanced scalar extension.

proof.text: Construct the right quotient map by transposing the extension unit across the restriction-composition isomorphism, then use the transported restriction square. Its local rule is p tensor s mapped to p tensor piB(s). Define the left map as b followed by the right map followed by bfin inverse. The assumed normalization of b and compatibility of cS,cB with piB give the left local rule. Cancellation of bfin inverse followed by bfin gives the quotient square.

source.place: Tags 03CY and 03EK; normalized extension/restriction adjunction and balanced scalar extension.

proof.text: Construct the right transition in the same way for qB, and identify the successive scalar restrictions by piB(n+1) followed by qB = piB(n). Define the left transition by conjugating the right transition by the finite comparisons. The identity qB*i(n+1)=i(n)*qA and the inverse cB transport square show its value on every nested pure tensor. Cancellation proves the transition square.

proof.text: All module constructions are natural transformations and natural isomorphisms. Apply Mathlib NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex and NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex termwise, so naturality gives compatibility with differentials and with every chain map. Functor compositions can be normalized before lifting since the two presentations are definitionally equal. No boundedness, flatness or surjectivity is used.

lean.statement:
theorem scalar_quotient_chain_squares (b : left g d ≅ right g d)
    (hb : UpperFormula g d b) :
    ∃ (bfin : ∀ n : ℕ, finiteLeft g d n ≅ finiteRight g d n)
      (v : ∀ n : ℕ, left g d ⟶ restrictedLeft g d n)
      (w : ∀ n : ℕ, right g d ⟶ restrictedRight g d n)
      (vtrans : ∀ n : ℕ, restrictedLeft g d (Nat.succ n) ⟶ restrictedLeft g d n)
      (wtrans : ∀ n : ℕ, restrictedRight g d (Nat.succ n) ⟶ restrictedRight g d n),
      FiniteFormulas g d bfin ∧ QuotientFormulas g d v w ∧
      TransitionFormulas g d vtrans wtrans ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ,
        v n ≫ Functor.whiskerRight (bfin n).hom
          (scalarRestrict.{t, r, max r (t + 1)} X (DX.piB n)) =
          b.hom ≫ w n) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ,
        vtrans n ≫ Functor.whiskerRight (bfin n).hom
          (scalarRestrict.{t, r, max r (t + 1)} X (DX.piB n)) =
          Functor.whiskerRight (bfin (Nat.succ n)).hom
            (scalarRestrict.{t, r, max r (t + 1)} X (DX.piB (Nat.succ n))) ≫ wtrans n)
lean.note: Uses the canonical corresponding-object inverse-image model and the existing balanced scalar-extension functor, specialized with explicit independent universes. Tower and Transport only bundle the stated hypotheses. Positive level m is n+1; comparisons are natural B_X,m-linear cochain isomorphisms, with both inverse rules and quotient/transition natural-transformation squares. No flatness or surjectivity assumptions.
